**What was fixed:**

1. **Views limit.** `MAX_VIEWS` is now 16; the viewer's biggest layout is 12 views. Each view now has its own set of parameter slots, sized to match. The layout never asks for more than the limit: after the game's views it fits the pane, then the magnifier, then the insets in order. Insets left out take no clicks, and both the layout and the renderer log the overflow once instead of every frame.
2. **Screen magnifier.** It copies a rectangle around the pointer, kept inside the window, and its box now sits beside that rectangle, so it never copies its own frame. Clicks on it map to the same source. Live: no black columns.
3. **City screen's map with a split (ui=window).** The game's other views (the city map) and its interface are now drawn after the pane and insets, with their own camera, and clicks there go to the game. With ui=pane and a city screen open, the screen is now fitted too; before, it was drawn unfitted.
4. **Sharp text under fog.** This is the full fix, not the labels-only fallback. A zoomed view is drawn at zoom 1 and scaled up to its first zoomed sprite. From there on, the rest of it is drawn at its zoom straight into the target, pixel-exact with the scaled picture, so zoomed text stays in its pass and the fog darkens it. The shaders and the reference implement this the same way. Live: fogged labels are about as dark with sharp text as with pixel text (Konigsberg 84 vs 88).
5. **Minimap rectangles in ui=pane.** I fixed this in the viewer, so no `mark_views` change was needed. The fitted screen's interface is drawn as a "hairline" view: anything the downscaling would shrink to nothing keeps one screen pixel. Live: all yellow rectangles are complete.
6. **Ctrl+Shift+Space.** It releases the mouse if captured. If free, it captures only when the view under the pointer follows the world cursor; otherwise it does nothing. Every change is logged ("viewer: mouse captured …", "mouse released …", "mouse stays free …"), and losing focus releases it too.
7. **Free pane starting black.** The title screen does have an empty game view looking at (0, 0), so "first world view" alone was not enough. A free view now waits until the scene has a world. It then follows the middle of the game's view for about 3 s (180 frames) and is fixed after that, unless you move it by hand first; the placement is logged. Live, loading a save moved the game's view twice (first to (2302, 2332)) before it settled at (2240, 1440), which is where the pane ended up.

**Tests added:**
- GPU-vs-reference: drawing at the zoom equals the scaled picture (five zooms, a fitted screen and an inset, both colour models), a label darkened by a later pass, hairlines at 1/2 and 1/3, and 12 views all drawn.
- Layout: all views fit the limit (and what gets left out), the city map over the pane, a city screen fitted into the pane, the free pane placement, the magnifier never copying itself, and the Space toggle. The existing magnifier test was updated: the box now sits at x 354 instead of 324.

**One thing I noticed but left alone:** in ui=pane, the part of the main pane below the fitted screen still counts as "the game's screen". A click or a new inset there maps to a point past the bottom of the game's window.

**1. Edge scroll.**
- **Cause:** the game never reads the mouse messages for this. On a 66 ms timer, the function at 0x4DE4F0 checks `GetFocus` (the exe's only call) and gets the pointer from jgl.dll's `GetCursorPos` (jgl's only call). It scrolls within 16 px of an edge, faster nearer.
- **Viewer side:** it now sends a new `Input::Edge` (wire v17) when the pointer rests at the window edge. It only does so over the game's main view at zoom 1 and unmoved, not with `ui=pane`, and with a split only at the main pane's outer edges. It clears when the pointer leaves the window or the window loses focus.
- **Bridge side:** while that holds, the bridge makes those two imports report the game's pointer at the same distance from the game's edge, with the game window focused. This goes through a new safe module, `inproc::pointer`, plus a guarded write in `inproc::mem`.
- **Live check:** pointer at (1919,540), (0,540) and (960,1079) for 3.5 s scrolled the camera in both modes; (960,0) was checked in-process only. The middle of the screen and a zoomed main view did not scroll.
- **Side effect:** while the pointer sits at the edge, the game's tooltips and held-button repeat also see the fake position.

**2. Bridge log.** It now says "renderer native: …" or "renderer in-process: …". In native mode the viewer's own log lines from info up are copied into civ3-bridge.log under `civ3r_native`, so the "using adapter … RADV … (Vulkan)" and "viewer adapter" lines are there. A line repeated many times is written once with a count.

**3. Glyph sheets.**
- `tools/gen-civ3-fonts` now makes every size from 5 to 48 px, plus 54, 56, 60, 64, 72, 80, 84 and 96. I ran it in a throwaway VM (4 GB, 800×600) and added 120 sheets to `~/.cache/civ3r/fonts`.
- Any other size is drawn at the nearest one there is, logged once per size; requests above 96 px are capped at 96. A font that fails to load is warned about once, not once per colour.
- A test checks that every game text size at every zoom step has a sheet.
- With a split, `ui=pane` and a 3× pane, there were no font WARNs in either mode. The only note was one info line ("size 4, drawn at 5").

**4. Install scripts.** `tools/install-native` and `tools/install-bridge` now use `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; I used them for all my installs.

**5. Modal log.** A selection the game refuses is now logged as "the game refused to select unit 357 at (18, 34) (no moves left?); selected: Some(175)". This has a unit test only; I didn't reproduce it live.

**6. First-open lag.**
- **Where the time went:** each rebuild was a full atlas compile on the publishing thread. That took about 2 s in the native-mode bridge and 3–4 s under the old WoW64. The native viewer then compiled its own copy, also blocking that thread. On top came the 2 s wait between rebuilds and several rebuild rounds per screen. Scenes published in between had no art for the screen, which was the black panels.
- **What changed:**
  - A rebuild now runs on its own thread once requests settle (about 70–300 ms), while the old art keeps being published.
  - In native mode the bridge builds only the sprite tables, from file headers. The viewer gets the description at once and compiles it on its own thread at the same time, re-cutting only sheets it hasn't seen.
  - In-process, the bridge compiles from a cache of the previous compile's sheets. Its working set peaked at 1042 MiB, slightly lower than without the cache.
  - While a screen's art is missing, the bridge holds the scene back (at most 4 s). The viewer keeps drawing its last complete frame, including the layout of its views, until the new art arrives.

| One rebuild, native viewer | 0.3–0.45 s | 0.11–0.25 s |
| One rebuild, in-process | 3–4 s (my intermediate build, not the baseline) | 200–430 ms |

- **Further speed-up:** half the remaining time is parsing the 2.9 MB description, mostly one table per glyph. Packing each font into a single sheet would be the next step.

**Outside the bridge crates.** These fixes needed small changes in crates the other agent also works in, so expect merge conflicts there:
- `scene`: the new `Input::Edge` and the wire version bump to 17.
- `tile-viewer/layout.rs`: the edge detection.
- `tile-viewer/lib.rs`: CursorLeft/focus handling, keeping the last frame while art is pending, and the upload-time log.
- `render-desc`: the cached and tables-only compiles.

**How it works**
- **Renderer:** each sprite now stores its sample box, its scaling mode and an optional twin to draw instead. A camera has a `downscale` value. In that mode `tile_vs` and `free_vs` place the shrunk quad and the fragment shaders read texel `box + n·(i, j)`. The reference renderer does exactly the same. Screen-space sprites are not shrunk.
- **Where halving lives:** the world stays at full size. The view scales the grid steps, divides layer offsets and world sprite positions (rounded toward zero, as C divides), and keeps its camera and cull rectangle in its own pixels. The viewer's own zoom applies on top, so a zoomed-out view shown at 2× in a pane works.
- **render-desc:** compiling finds each sprite's box once, from the full-size pixels and the blank load. A `scaled_origin` cell goes into the atlas as the sprite's twin. `scaled_down`, the sheet's `downscale` key and the CPU shrinking are gone. The old shrink code is kept only inside the tests, with a note.
- **Scene and wire:** views carry their downscale (wire version 19). The viewer passes it to its pane, insets, magnifier, world bounds and markers.
- **civ3-bridge:** zoomed out, it sends the game view and the city view with downscale 2 and no longer recompiles. District slices are described for both zooms up front; all district sheets now keep their anchor when shrunk. City labels are laid out in zoomed-out pixels, so the bridge doubles their positions and the renderer halves them back. The native viewer and civ3-tool also build one copy of the art.

- **Tests:** `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` (radv) passes, and so does `cargo check -p civ3-bridge --target i686-pc-windows-gnu`. New GPU-vs-reference tests cover downscale 2 and 3, both colour models, wrapping, culling, clipped and darkening free sprites, twins, empty boxes, and a half-size view at zoom 2/1 and 3/2. A new render-desc test draws a sheet both ways (old CPU shrink vs. reference and GPU at downscale 2): the pixels are identical.
- **Same frames as before:** civ3-tool renders of the five zoomed-out traces match the old build exactly for N03, A03 and L3. M1 and M2 differ in about 250 pixels in the bottom-right interface panel: the unit picture there is no longer shrunk, which brings it closer to the game.
